title: Perimeter Sentinel: Terraform module for VPC security controls (SGs, NACLs, private DNS, egress governance)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a reusable Terraform module (Perimeter Sentinel) that codifies Redwood's recommended VPC perimeter controls for Private deployments. The module must provide opinionated defaults while allowing customization for multi-account, multi-AZ deployments. Core capabilities: managed security groups with tag-based inheritance and least-privilege defaults; stateless NACL scaffolding to protect subnets (with sane defaults and explicit deny/allow rules); private DNS automation (Route53 private hosted zones, conditional forwarding for shared services); and egress governance patterns (prefix-list driven egress allow lists, optional egress-proxy/NAT routing, and enforced route table attachments). The module should include upgrade hooks and a clear migration path from legacy modules, built-in health checks (CloudWatch metrics and Route53 health checks for egress-proxy endpoints), and CI acceptance tests. The output must be Terraform Registry–ready with versioning, changelog, and a deprecation policy for breaking changes.
acceptance_criteria: Module publishes to internal registry with semantic versioning and CHANGELOG.md
Default deployment creates least-privilege SGs: no 0.0.0.0/0 ingress except admin-bastion and documented exceptions
NACLs created for public/private subnets with explicit ephemeral port allowances and documented audit rules
Private hosted zone created and optionally delegated to org shared-services; DNS records can be bootstrapped via module inputs
Egress can be toggled between NAT gateway path and egress-proxy path; policy enforced via route table attachments and prefix-lists
Automated CI tests validate common misconfigurations (open SGs, missing route to egress proxy, incorrect NACL order)
Upgrade guide included for migrating state from legacy-perimeter module (state-move commands documented)
Security review completed and sign-off obtained before release to production customers
implementation_notes: Expose inputs: allowed_egress_prefix_list_ids, egress_mode (nat|proxy), enable_private_dns (bool), sg_tags, assume_role_arn for cross-account installs
Prefer AWS managed prefix lists for egress allow lists to simplify updates across accounts; provide helper script to push updates to managed prefix lists
Implement default-deny SG baseline with explicit reusable inbound/outbound rule blocks; encourage use of module 'attach-sg' helper for app stacks
NACL ordering is deterministic: create ordered rule indices with gaps to allow safe insertions during upgrades
Private DNS: create Route53 private hosted zone and optional record set module; support delegation via hosted zone associations for other accounts
Health checks: synthesize CloudWatch metrics for egress failures and a Route53 health check for the egress-proxy endpoint; wire alarm to Ops PagerDuty via existing SNS topic
State migration: provide terraform state mv examples and an automated helper (scripts/migrate_state.sh) to move legacy resources to new module names
Testing: use terratest for functional tests in CI and checkov/conftest policy checks in pre-commit
migration_plan: Provide a two-step upgrade: (1) v1 -> v1.1 non-breaking release with new outputs and prefix-list support; (2) v2 breaking changes (NACL rule index schema change) which requires state migration. Document exact terraform state mv commands for each resource type and include small helper scripts. Offer a canary rollout pattern in Dedicated environments: apply module to a single VPC, validate telemetry for 72 hours, then roll out org-wide. Deprecate legacy module names at v2.1 with a grace period of 90 days.
tests: CI pipeline: terratest suite runs in sandbox account and must pass before tag/registry publish
Policy tests: conftest + cfn-nag style checks for Terraform JSON plan outputs
Security smoke tests: script verifies no SG ingress 0.0.0.0/0, verified route tables have egress path, and Route53 private hosted zone resolves expected names
Chaos test: simulate egress-proxy failure and assert N+1 fallback behavior to NAT or alternate region per routing policy
